Projects.Title: AHEPA Website Redesign
Projects.Desc: I redesigned the website for the Ottawa chapter of AHEPA (American Hellenic Educational Progressive Association) to modernize their online presence and better serve their mission of promoting Hellenism in Ottawa. I worked from the ground up, identifying core requirements with stakeholders, providing various design alternatives in Figma, implementing the redesign using Square Online, iterating based on stakeholder feedback, and creating documentation for future upkeep.
Projects.ShortDesc: Redesigned the Ottawa AHEPA chapter website to modernize their digital presence.

Image.alt: The redesigned AHEPA Ottawa homepage now features a modern layout with improved navigation and upcoming events posted front and center.
Figma design alternatives for the site banner, colour palettes and typography were presented to stakeholders.
Mockups of site pages with notes were created in Figma to demonstrate information architecture.
Documentation guide created for stakeholders outlining key Square Online features and best practices for future site upkeep.

Projects.Title: The Little Robot
Projects.Desc: The Little Robot is a linear 3D platforming and melee combat game where you play as a small robot trapped in an isolated testing facility, unaware of the world beyond its walls. I led a team of 6 through an 8-month Capstone project in Unity, handling core game infrastructure, creating environmental scripting of elements such as the conveyor belts, and implementing cutscene sequences and cameras.
Projects.ShortDesc: Led the creation of a 3D platforming game, tackling the core infrastructure, environmental, and camera implementation.

Image.alt: The robot must traverse through platforming sections as he descends deeper into the facility.
Explore a mysterious facility where dangerous fungus runs rampant.
The robot must defeat a dangerous reoccuring enemy with its fast-paced attacks.

Projects.Title: Portfolio
Projects.Desc: I created this portfolio website to initially showcase some of the projects I've created through university. It has since evolved (and will continue to do so), as I grow my skills. The site was designed in Figma, built with React, and although initially styled with plain CSS, it has since been updated to use Tailwind.
Projects.ShortDesc: A portfolio site created with React and Tailwind to showcase my projects and skills.

Image.alt: The homepage was designed to showcase my style and be UX-forward, while displaying my skills and accomplishments.
The previous homepage of my portfolio simply served as a landing page, and forced the user to navigate through different pages with the top navbar.
The responsive design of the site was taken into consideration.
Mockups were created in Figma, and were used as a basis for iteration during the development phase.

Projects.Title: Crab Cove
Projects.Desc: Crab Cove is a relaxing game about a crab collecting items to decorate his sandcastle! Created by a team of 4 to fulfill the challenge of making a unique player controller in Unity, I was responsible for developing the crab's sideways movement and item spawning with C#, as well as the camerawork.
Projects.ShortDesc: A relaxing crab game created in Unity.

Image.alt: The crab can run around a map finding treasures to bring back to his home.
Digging holes in the sand will help the crab find treasures!
The crab can pick up his treasures with either claw to bring them back to his sandcastle home and decorate it.

Projects.Title: Garden Planner
Projects.Desc: I created the Garden Planner in university with a Django backend and a React frontend. It allows users to plan out their gardens by specifying the dimensions and amount of sun and using the OpenFarm API to suggest possible plants to grow. Users can then save these plants to their gardens and be notified when they should be watered and harvested. User accounts are also saved to the database so that users can login and logout at any time.
Projects.ShortDesc: Created a garden planner with Django and React that allows users to manage plants in gardens with specified criteria.

Image.alt: Users can create and update garden specifications from the main page.
Viewing a garden allows users to see the existing plants and see possible new ones that fit the garden criteria from the OpenFarm API.
Users can view all of the notifications from their gardens.

Projects.Title: Hangman
Projects.Desc: A game of hangman created with React that can be played in the browser. It leverages the Wikipedia API to provide the player with a random Wikipedia article title to guess. The UI is influenced by the video game Persona 5, which also makes use of tarot cards like the Hanged Man. It has been restructured many times as my knowledge of best practices improve.
Projects.ShortDesc: A game of hangman created with React that can be played in the browser.

Image.alt: All English letters (Aa-Zz) are hidden from the player. Any irregular letters, numbers, or punctuation characters are shown.
Players can choose to play on 3 difficulty modes. Easy allows 10 incorrect guesses, Hard allows 5 guesses and None allows infinite.
Once the title has been successfully guessed, or a game over is triggered, the player is able to travel to the corresponding Wikipedia article.

Projects.Title: OC Transpo Redesign
Projects.Desc: A redesign of several pages of the OC Transpo site as it is a frequently used service for university students and the site had many areas for improvement. We conducted user surveys and accessibility checks to find pain points, brainstormed to create mid-fidelity mockups in Figma and documented the process in a written report.
Projects.ShortDesc: A redesign of several pages of the OC Transpo site through user-testing and Figma mockups.

Image.alt: The existing site was analyzed using the WAVE accessibility checker and various screen readers after which a detailed document of errors and warnings was written.
User survey and think-aloud sessions were conducted with university-age participants to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the existing site.
New designs were drawn with pen and paper to resolve the main issues found in the analysis phase.
Mid-fidelity mockups of several key pages were created in Figma to demonstrate the new design.

Projects.Title: Nature Museum Whale App
Projects.Desc: An interactive application to better immerse visitors at the Canadian Museum of Nature by leading users to certain exhibits via an AR whale on the screen and progressively louder whale calls as they get closer to the exhibit. Significant user testing and analysis was conducted before suitable design alternatives were brainstormed. A low fidelity design was created in Figma and tested with users before creating a mid-fidelity prototype.
Projects.ShortDesc: An interactive AR application was designed in Figma to immerse visitors at the Canadian Museum of Nature.

Image.alt: User survey and think-aloud sessions were conducted with users of various ages to identify what features would be most engaging. User personas and scenarios were also created to better understand our target audience.
Initial designs were drawn with pen and paper to satisfy the criteria of the user tests.
Low-fidelity mockups of the app design were created in Figma before being tested again by users.
A final mid-fidelity prototype was created based on the low-fidelity feedback.
Our mid-fidelity prototype was created in Figma and shown to the many users we tested.

Projects.Title: Persona 3 Background
Projects.Desc: A computer background created using Vue.js and deployed to Wallpaper Engine. Initially created using vanilla JavaScript a few years ago, it has been recreated with Vue to improve the cleanliness of the code. The UI imitates that of the video game Persona 3 Portable where it displays the current date, the time of day, the phase of the moon and indicates how many days are left until a full moon. The background images are pulled directly from the PSP version's game files.
Projects.ShortDesc: A Persona 3 styled computer background that displays the date and the phase of the moon.

Image.alt: Times of day are displayed along with the date. These include After School (the game characters attend high school) Morning, Lunch, Evening and Late Night.
More memorable phases of the moon, such as Quarter, Half and Full moons are spelled out. Other moon phases have the number of days until a full moon beside it.
Notable times of day and background images are different during weekends.
Following with the game, the 'hidden 25th hour' after midnight changes the UI to green. This occurs here between midnight and 1am.

Projects.Title: Event Scheduler
Projects.Desc: This Proof-of-Concept mobile application was created as an event scheduler that allows users to view, add, update, delete events, and notify users of upcoming events. Multiple early designs that fit the specifications along with standard mobile app design theories were considered. The final design was then created using Android Studio with Java. The app is not fully functional, but it does demonstrate the intended design and functionality, including multiple pages with Android Fragments, and data storage with ViewModels.
Projects.ShortDesc: An event scheduler mobile app created using Android Studio.

Image.alt: Many designs were drawn out on paper, and the best few were created as wireframes in Balsamiq.
The wireframe designs were put into a predictive modelling program to estimate task times.
The final design was created in Android Studio and tested with a virtual device.

Projects.Title: Flower Flux
Projects.Desc: Help Gatsbee the bee pollinate the flowers in his garden! This 2D side-scrolling game was created in a group of 4 during university with Unity. I was responsible for the side scrolling, the UI and menu scripting as well as the pollination ability.
Projects.ShortDesc: A 2D side-scroller game created with Unity.

Image.alt: Fly around as Gatsbee the bee to each of your flowers and pollinate them.
Players must juggle the timers of each flower to prevent them from dying.
Each level adds new flowers of increasing difficulties.

Projects.Title: Crow Game & Controller
Projects.Desc: A custom controller and accomanying game creating using Arduino and it's StandardFirmata library along with the C++ openFrameworks library. The crow-shaped controller controls a crow on screen with the goal of bringing items back to its nest. The Arduino UNO controller has an IR sensor underneath to detect height, a pressure sensor in each wing to allow players to hold and carry items, a button on each wing to flip the crow's direction on screen, and an RGB LED as each eye to indicate various states within the game.
Projects.ShortDesc: A crow-shaped controller and accompanying game created using Arduino and it's StandardFirmata library along with the C++ openFrameworks library

Image.alt: Players are tasked with picking up items of various 'weights' and returning them to their nest to gather points.
The crow on screen detects the height of the controller.
The controller is powered by an Arduino UNO, and the casing is created with cardboard, plastic squeeze bottles, foam and black tape.
